expectations.text: States that instructions to a model are not enforcement, regardless of wording or emphasis
expectations.evidence: "it doesn't matter how emphatically it's phrased, because the agent isn't consulting a rule at the moment it acts, it's pattern-matching on a compacted memory"

expectations.text: Redirects away from rewording CLAUDE.md as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "The fix is to move both rules off rung 0 (prose) onto rung 1 (control)"

expectations.text: Recommends permission deny rules in settings.json with concrete syntax
expectations.evidence: Provides JSON with Bash(git push --force:*), Edit(./src/generated/**), Write(./src/generated/**)

expectations.text: Recommends a PreToolUse hook for cases that need logic rather than a pattern match
expectations.evidence: Does not mention PreToolUse hooks at all

expectations.text: Explains that the deny message should say what to do instead, not merely refuse
expectations.evidence: "worth writing something like 'Blocked: force-push is disabled on this repo. If you need to rewrite remote history, ask the user to run it themselves.'"

expectations.text: Recommends verifying the device actually fires rather than assuming it works
expectations.evidence: Does not recommend testing or verifying the device

expectations.text: Recommends committing the rules so they apply to the whole team, not just one machine
expectations.evidence: Does not mention committing settings.json; only mentions server-side branch protection

expectations.text: Explains why repetition and capitals do not make an instruction reliable
expectations.evidence: "That ~1-in-10 failure rate isn't a fluke, it's the expected failure rate for training-based enforcement — it doesn't matter how emphatically it's phrased"
